title: OpenAI — Prompt caching
supported_point: Cache behavior and usage mappings are model/API-dependent. Where cache-write tokens are reported inside input, ordinary input subtracts both cached reads and writes. Separate those categories and preserve the native usage object.
limit: Official reference; inspected on 2026-09-20. Do not apply newer-model fields to every compatible endpoint.

title: Anthropic — Prompt caching
supported_point: Explicit pre-warming uses a provider request; local compilation alone is not a cache write. Total input combines ordinary, cache-read and cache-creation fields.
limit: Official reference; inspected on 2026-09-20. Pre-warming is not introduced as a required ASTROLABE workflow.

title: OpenAI — Function calling
supported_point: The function-call exchange retains native assistant output and pairs each tool result with its call ID.
limit: Official protocol documentation; inspected on 2026-09-20. The revised pseudocode is illustrative, not an SDK implementation.

title: OpenAI — Conversation state
supported_point: Continuation reduces retransmission, not the obligation to account for effective history; chained previous input remains billable.
limit: Official reference; inspected on 2026-09-20. Reduction must not reintroduce unwanted old history through provider state.

title: Git — git-worktree
supported_point: Ordinary refs are shared across linked worktrees; per-worker shadow refs therefore require a distinct namespace. Worktree separation is not an OS capability boundary.
limit: Official documentation; inspected on 2026-09-20. Workspace suffix is this revision’s engineering inference.

title: Git — git-update-ref
supported_point: Ref updates can verify an expected old object ID. That protects publication of the ref, not atomic restoration of every file.
limit: Official documentation; inspected on 2026-09-20. Filesystem restoration still needs guarded recovery.

title: SQLite — Atomic Commit
supported_point: SQLite’s commit guarantees concern its database and documented storage assumptions, not arbitrary repository mutations or remote effects.
limit: Official engineering documentation; inspected on 2026-09-20. No new transaction framework was inferred.

title: MCP — Tools specification, 2025-06-18
supported_point: Tool annotations from untrusted servers are not trusted authority. A read-only hint cannot grant an executor capability.
limit: Pinned official specification version; inspected on 2026-09-20. This is not a claim that every later MCP capability was audited.

title: The Complexity Trap, arXiv:2508.21433v3
supported_point: Observation masking is a meaningful baseline; hybrid comparisons are workload-specific. The paper does not make deterministic rebuilding universally optimal.
limit: Primary research, version pinned; inspected on 2026-09-20. Deterministic rebuilding remains the authoritative baseline choice; no summarizer was added.

title: SoL-Pi, arXiv:2609.20519v1
supported_point: The complete efficiency configuration and highest-scoring configuration are different operating points. Their largest savings and best quality cannot be combined into one result.
limit: Primary research, version pinned; inspected on 2026-09-20. Reported findings do not validate ASTROLABE or establish a universal fusion policy.

title: The Missing Complement, arXiv:2609.20050v1
supported_point: Constructed-pool evidence coverage and gold-blind repository discovery are different claims. Complementary retrieval is useful motivation, not proof of end-to-end repair success.
limit: Primary research, version pinned; inspected on 2026-09-20. No additional retrieval-agent orchestration was adopted.
